To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical region of the QCD critical endpoint is much wider than the mean-field region and that the backreaction of matter fluctuations on the Yang-Mills system leads to a shift of the critical point towards lower chemical potentials.

(1) the critical exponents of the critical region are strongly path dependent and that the renormalized critical exponents are significantly different from the mean-field ones; (2) the renormalization procedure leads to a reduction of the critical region and a shift in the position of the critical point; and (3) the higher-order generalized quarks-number susceptibilities are strongly enhanced near the critical endpoint and their sign structure is a sensitive probe of the critical point

the critical endpoint is shifted toward higher baryonic chemical potentials when Polyakov loops are included in the effective chiral models and that the sign structure of the higher-order moments is modified in the vicinity of the critical point.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the QCD critical region and with the investigation of the higher-order moments of event-byevent distributions in the QCD phase transition.
the study of the QCD critical point and its vicinity, as well as with the investigation of higher-order moments as possible probes of the critical region in heavy-ion collisions.
the study of critical phenomena in QCD, with a focus on the QCD critical endpoint and the higher moments of the event-by-event distributions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical region in the phase diagram of (2 + 2)- and (2 + 3)-flavor models is rather small.
the critical point is a very interesting object in the phase diagram of QCD, and its location is still a matter of discussion.
the QCD phase structure is very rich and that a critical endpoint is most likely to be present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a critical region is present in the (2 + 3)-flavor model and that the renormalization effects are rather moderate.
we find that higher order cumulants of the quark-number fluctuations are enhanced at the critical endpoint and that the backreaction of matter fluctuations on the gluonic sector is not significant.
the critical region in the (μ B, T) phase diagram is rather large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical region is much smaller in the presence of the Polyakov loop than in the chiral model alone.
the renormalized critical region is much smaller than that obtained within mean-field approximations.
the renormalization of the effective chiral (3 + 1)- and (2 + 0)-flavor models is crucial for the determination of the location of the critical point in the phase diagram.
